title: SKILL.md frontmatter
description: The YAML frontmatter block at the top of every SKILL.md. This is the machine view of a skill: who may run it, what it needs, whether it is reproducible, and which contract it satisfies. The procedure itself is NOT here — it stays in the standard operating procedure page named by `sop`, which remains the single source of truth for narrative. The body below the frontmatter carries only what the contract needs and the SOP does not say.

id.description: Level-qualified skill id, matching its folder path under skills/.

description.description: One sentence. Used for routing without reading the body, so it must say what the skill does, not what area it is about.

expert.description: The expert bundle this skill belongs to.

determinism.description: deterministic: reproducible, same inputs give the same bytes, runs freely. judgment: something is being decided, so the result is a diff and a reason, never a silent write. A conforming runtime surfaces this before execution, not after.

roles.description: Role ids permitted to run this skill. Resolved against registry/roles/.

degradation.description: What to do when the capability is absent. fail: stop and say so, never substitute an approximation. warn: log and continue. skip: omit the dependent step. fallback: use fallbackId.

satisfies.description: Requirement ids or requirement statement keys this skill discharges.

routingPatterns.description: Regular expressions matching requests this skill handles. Matched case-insensitively by convention, so patterns must not carry an inline flag group: JavaScript rejects the PCRE (?i) prefix outright, and a pattern that fails to compile silently routes nothing.

sop.description: Repository path to the standard operating procedure page holding this skill's procedure — normally under input/pagecontent. The SOP is the single source of truth for narrative and this skill does not restate it; an agent reads both. Required, because a skill whose procedure is nowhere is not a skill.

alsoRead.description: Further SOP pages this skill depends on but does not own, such as authoring_conventions.md or versioning.md.

status.description: Describes the contract, not the narrative. specified: the input and output schemas constrain real structure and a requirement file carries the definition of done. placeholder: the schemas permit anything and no requirement file exists yet, so validating against them is not evidence of a correct artifact. Both kinds point at a real SOP and are usable by a person today.

then.description: A specified contract must name the requirement its output is checked against, or nothing distinguishes it from a placeholder.
